content.definition: A hierarchical data structure where each node has at most two children, referred to as left and right child. Forms the foundation for many advanced tree structures.
key_properties: Each node has at most two children
Unique path between any two nodes

full_binary_tree.description: Every node has either 0 or 2 children
properties: Maximizes internal nodes for given height

complete_binary_tree.description: All levels filled except possibly the last, which fills left to right

perfect_binary_tree.description: All internal nodes have 2 children and all leaves at same level

balanced_binary_tree.description: Height difference between left and right subtrees ≤ 1 for all nodes

level_order.order: Level by level, left to right

insertion.description: Add new node maintaining tree properties

deletion.description: Remove node while preserving tree structure

search.complexity: O(h) for BST, O(n) for general binary tree

time_complexities.search: O(h) - path from root to target

interview_strategies: Always consider both recursive and iterative approaches
Consider what information needs to be passed up/down the tree
Draw small examples to understand the pattern
Consider edge cases: empty tree, single node, skewed tree
optimization_techniques: Iterative solutions to avoid stack overflow
